name: ADP2302ARDZ-5.0-R7
title: ADP2302/ADP2303: 2 A / 3 A, 20 V, 700 kHz non-synchronous step-down regulators
summary: A pair of non-synchronous buck regulators with the high-side power MOSFET and bootstrap diode on chip: the ADP2302 delivers up to 2 A and the ADP2303 up to 3 A, from a 3.0 V to 20 V input. They switch at a fixed 700 kHz under peak current-mode control, compensated inside, and drop into pulse skipping at light load. Each comes adjustable down to 0.8 V (±1.5 % reference over temperature) or fixed at 2.5 V, 3.3 V or 5.0 V; the ADP2302ARDZ-5.0-R7 is the 2 A part fixed at 5.0 V on tape and reel. A precision enable with hysteresis, power-good output, soft start, UVLO, overcurrent limit with frequency foldback, overvoltage protection and thermal shutdown are built in; the package is an 8-lead SOIC with exposed pad, rated for -40 °C to +125 °C junction.
key_figures: adjustable from 0.8 V, or fixed 2.5 V, 3.3 V, 5.0 V
4.925 V min, 5.0 V typ, 5.075 V max

pins.name: BST
pins.function: Supply for the high-side switch driver. A 0.1 µF capacitor from BST to SW gives the driver its floating supply.

pins.name: VIN
pins.function: Input supply. Decouple it to GND with a ceramic capacitor placed right at the pin.

pins.name: EN
pins.function: Enable. High turns the output on, low turns it off. With a resistor divider it works as an adjustable undervoltage lockout. A 1.2 µA current inside pulls it to GND.

pins.name: FB
pins.function: Feedback sense. On the adjustable part it takes the tap of a resistor divider from the output; on the fixed-output parts it ties straight to the output.

pins.name: NC
pins.function: Reserved for factory test. Tie it to GND or leave it open.

pins.name: GND
pins.function: Ground; connect to the ground plane.

pins.name: SW
pins.function: Switch node. The inductor runs from SW to the output and the catch diode from SW to GND.

pins.name: EPAD
pins.function: Exposed pad on the underside. Solder it to a ground plane below the chip to carry heat away.

notes: Pins 1 to 4 run down one side (BST, VIN, EN, PGOOD) and pins 8 to 5 down the other (SW, GND, NC, FB), seen from the top; the exposed pad is pin 9.

circuits.title: Typical application circuit
circuits.description: The basic arrangement for either part: an input capacitor at VIN, a bootstrap capacitor from BST to SW, a catch diode from SW to ground, an inductor from SW to the output with an output capacitor, and a two-resistor divider from the output to FB. EN is a logic on/off input and PGOOD an output.

circuits.title: External bootstrap circuit for low input voltage
circuits.description: For a 3.0 V to 5.0 V input: a Schottky diode from a separate 5 V bias supply into BST tops up the bootstrap capacitor so the high-side switch gets full gate drive. The rest is the usual buck: input capacitor, BST-SW capacitor, catch diode, inductor, output capacitor, feedback divider and an on/off EN input.
notes: The bias voltage stays below 5.5 V.

circuits.title: Design example: ADP2303, 12 V to 3.3 V at 3 A with 7.8 V start-up
circuits.description: ADP2303 steps 12 V down to 3.3 V at up to 3 A. CIN decouples the input, CBST feeds the high-side driver from SW, and the SSB43L Schottky catches the inductor current while the switch is off; L (4.7 µH) and 47 µF + 47 µF of output capacitance filter the output. EN sits on a divider from VIN (REN1 56 kΩ over REN2 10.2 kΩ), so the converter waits until VIN reaches about 7.8 V. RPGOOD pulls the open-drain PGOOD up to VIN. RTOP and RBOT divide the output onto FB to set 3.3 V.

operation.text: A non-synchronous buck converter: the high-side power MOSFET and its bootstrap diode are inside, the catch diode and the LC filter outside. It runs from 3.0 V to 20 V in and regulates down to 0.8 V. The ADP2302 is rated for 2 A of continuous load and the ADP2303 for 3 A. Control is fixed-frequency peak current mode at 700 kHz with internal compensation and internal slope compensation, which keeps the loop free of subharmonic oscillation at duty cycles near or above 50 %.

Each oscillator cycle turns the MOSFET on, and inductor current climbs until the sensed current reaches the peak set by the error amplifier; the switch then opens and the current falls through the external diode until the next clock edge. Duty cycle sets the output.

At light load the part moves smoothly into pulse skipping: when the output sags below regulation it switches for a few PWM cycles, then idles with the switch off while the output capacitor carries the load. Regulation becomes hysteretic and the ripple is larger than in PWM mode. The comparator watches the internal compensation node, so the load at which skipping starts depends on VIN, VOUT, the inductor and the output capacitor.

An internal boot regulator holds BST about 5.0 V above SW (4.7 V to 5.3 V at VIN = 12 V) to drive the high-side gate, using a 0.1 µF X5R or X7R ceramic capacitor between BST and SW. The switch needs at least 1.2 V between BST and SW to turn on. An on-chip diode blocks reverse voltage from BST to VIN while the switch conducts. If BST is fed from an outside source through a diode, that voltage stays under 5.5 V.

Between 3 V and 5 V in, the boot regulator's dropout leaves too little gate drive, the MOSFET's on resistance rises and less load current is available. A small-signal Schottky diode from an external 5.0 V bias into BST restores the drive; the bias stays below 5.5 V since BST to SW is rated to 6 V.

For stable light-load operation and for start-up into a pre-biased output, VIN must exceed the regulated (or pre-bias) output by more than 2.1 V worst case. With less headroom the bootstrap capacitor charges only when some minimum load current flows.

The 170 ns worst-case minimum on time sets the lowest output for a given highest input; the 280 ns worst-case minimum off time and the bootstrap dropout set the highest output for a given lowest input.

EN turns the part on above 1.2 V (typical) and off below 1.1 V, a 100 mV hysteresis. An internal 1.2 µA pull-down holds a floating EN low. EN may simply be tied to VIN so that the part starts when power arrives. A divider from VIN to EN makes an adjustable UVLO, which avoids start-up trouble when VIN ramps slowly under a heavy load; a divider from another supply's output sequences the part after that supply.
A digital soft start inside ramps the output over a fixed 2048 clock cycles to limit inrush current. Soft start is also run on recovery from a hard short, from UVLO and from thermal shutdown.

Positive current through the high-side switch is limited (peak limit 3.5 A typical on the ADP2302, 5.5 A on the ADP2303). When FB falls the switching frequency folds back to 1/2, 1/4 and 1/8 of fSW, giving the inductor current more time to fall and lowering the average output current so it cannot run away. Clearing a hard short (VFB ≤ 0.2 V) starts a fresh soft-start ramp, which limits inrush and keeps the output from overshooting.
The UVLO is fixed inside: the part shuts down with the switch off when VIN falls below 2.4 V and starts a soft start once VIN rises above 2.7 V.
Above a 150 °C junction temperature the chip turns off; it restarts with a soft start after cooling below 135 °C (15 °C hysteresis).
If FB rises above 0.880 V, as when the output is shorted to a higher supply, the high-side switch is held off until FB drops back to 0.850 V, and normal operation then resumes.

PGOOD is open drain, high when good, and needs a pull-up resistor to a rail below 20.0 V. It goes high when FB is above 87.5 % of the reference and low when FB falls below 85 %; each change waits 32 cycles.

Inductances from 1 µH to 15 µH suit the part. A ripple of about 30 % of the highest load current is the usual compromise between transient response and efficiency. The inductor's current rating must exceed the peak current; a ferrite inductor that saturates sharply should have a saturation current above the switch current limit, checked with the output shorted over the temperature range. Larger inductors have lower DCR; core loss follows the ripple. Shielded ferrite cores are preferred for low core loss and low EMI.

The diode carries the inductor current while the switch is off, so its average current depends on duty cycle and load. A higher current rating is only needed for a shorted output, where diode current rises to the typical peak current limit. Its reverse voltage rating must exceed the highest input with margin for ringing at SW. A Schottky is preferred for its low forward drop and fast switching.

The input capacitor must handle the highest input voltage and an RMS ripple current of up to ILOAD(max)/2. X5R or X7R ceramic is preferred; 10 µF serves most designs. Place it as close to VIN as possible.

The output capacitor sets ripple and, with the inductor, the loop dynamics. The part is meant for small low-ESR, low-ESL ceramics, X5R or X7R; Y5V and Z5U are unsuitable because of their temperature and DC-bias behaviour. Most designs need at least 2 × 22 µF.

Dissipation inside the package is small at typical loads. At full load with high ambient temperature and high duty cycle the junction can pass 125 °C; at 150 °C the part shuts down and recovers below 135 °C.

12 V ± 10 % in, 3.3 V at 3 A out with 1 % ripple, start-up at about 7.8 V, PGOOD unused, so the ADP2303. With VD = 0.4 V the diode averages 2.1 A, so an SSB43L (4.0 A, 30 V) is chosen. The inductor equation gives 4.12 µH; 4.7 µH is the next standard value, giving 0.7 A ripple and a 3.4 A peak, so the VLF10040T-4R7N5R4. For 33 mV ripple with 3 mΩ ESR the ripple equation needs 4 µF, but loop stability and the recommended-components table lead to two 47 µF 6.3 V capacitors. RTOP = 31.6 kΩ and RBOT = 10.2 kΩ set 3.3 V. For VSTARTUP = 7.8 V with REN2 = 10.2 kΩ, REN1 comes to 56 kΩ.

Keep the input capacitor, inductor, catch diode, output capacitors and bootstrap capacitor close to the chip on short traces. The high-current loops (input capacitor, VIN, SW, inductor, diode, output capacitor and their ground return) should be short and wide. Use as much component-side ground copper as possible for heat, and a ground plane stitched to it with several vias. Keep the FB trace from the divider top to the output short and clear of high-current traces and the switch node. In the suggested placement the input capacitor sits by VIN and GND, the bootstrap capacitor and diode by SW and BST, and the inductor and output capacitors beyond them, with the exposed pad tied to ground.
